missing_supported_requirements.reason_missing_in_draft: Draft discloses many climate metrics, but does not clearly link metrics to 'each sustainability-related risk and opportunity that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s prospects' (i.e., risk/opportunity-by-risk/opportunity mapping).
Metrics are presented, but not explicitly identified as the metrics used to measure and monitor each specific sustainability-related risk/opportunity (no per-risk/opportunity articulation).

Some metrics/targets are not labelled/defined with clear, precise names/descriptions (e.g., 'All-scopes target (whole entity)' baseline value lacks unit/definition; internal carbon pricing table repeats 'Investment decisions' with different prices without clear differentiation).

Comparatives are not provided for all amounts disclosed (e.g., operational Scope 1/2/Scope 3 business travel are only shown for 2024; internal carbon prices only shown for 2024; high-carbon sector exposure only shown for 2024).

Draft mentions a correction to Scope 1 but does not provide revised comparative amounts for prior period estimates where new information relates to prior-period circumstances (if applicable) as required by B50(a).
No disclosure of the difference between previously disclosed comparative amounts and revised comparative amounts (if applicable).
No explanation of reasons for revising comparative amounts (if applicable) beyond a brief note about a correction to a pre-computed Scope 1 figure.
Draft indicates a correction to Scope 1 measurement but does not present revised comparative amounts (or state impracticability) consistent with B52(a) when a metric is redefined/replaced.
Changes to metrics/approach are not fully explained (only a brief correction note for Scope 1; no broader explanation of changes to approaches/inputs/assumptions where relevant).
Reasons for changes (and why the change provides more useful information) are not explained for the Scope 1 correction or any other metric changes.

Where new metrics appear to be introduced (e.g., internal carbon pricing, high-carbon sector exposure, carbon credit summary), no comparative amounts are provided and no impracticability statement is made.
Draft does not state that GHG emissions are measured in accordance with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004) or disclose an alternative required by a jurisdiction/exchange.

Operational GHG measurement approach, key inputs and assumptions are only partially described (Scope 2 market-based narrative mentions certificates/PPAs; Scope 1/Scope 3 business travel lack method/inputs/assumptions detail).
No explanation of why the chosen measurement approaches/inputs/assumptions were selected for Scope 1/2/3.
Draft notes a correction to Scope 1 but does not clearly describe changes to measurement approach/inputs/assumptions during the period and the reasons (beyond the brief correction statement).
No disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated accounting group and other investees (associates/JVs/unconsolidated subsidiaries) is provided.
No disclosure of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for 'other investees excluded from paragraph 29(a)(iv)' (i.e., outside consolidated group) is provided.
No explicit disclosure of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions attributable to associates, joint ventures and unconsolidated subsidiaries (if any) as part of required disaggregation.

Although location-based and market-based Scope 2 are disclosed, the disclosure about contractual instruments is incomplete (mentions RECs/PPAs generally but does not provide sufficient detail necessary to inform understanding, e.g., nature/volume/coverage where relevant).

Scope 3 categories included are not comprehensively disclosed with reference to the GHG Protocol Scope 3 categories; only business travel and financed emissions (Category 15) are shown, without stating whether other categories are excluded/not measured.

required_fixes: Add an explicit mapping of disclosed metrics/targets to the climate-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects (per-risk/opportunity identification).

Provide comparative information for the preceding period for all disclosed amounts, or explicitly state impracticability where applicable (do not add 'data unavailable' language unless it is true and supported elsewhere in the report payload).

If the Scope 1 'correction' relates to prior-period circumstances, disclose revised comparative amounts, the differences vs previously reported comparatives, and reasons (IFRS S1 B50/B52). If it does not, clarify it as a current-period correction without implying missing comparatives.

State the GHG emissions measurement standard used (GHG Protocol Corporate Standard 2004, unless another method is required) and describe measurement approaches, key inputs/assumptions, reasons for choices, and changes during the period (IFRS S2 29(a)(ii)–(iii)).

Disaggregate Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated accounting group and other investees as required by IFRS S2 29(a)(iv), or clarify that there are no such investees within scope (only if supported by the broader report payload).

Improve clarity/definitions for ambiguous items: define units and scope for the 'All-scopes target' baseline (120,000.0), and distinguish duplicated 'Investment decisions' internal carbon prices (e.g., different business lines/geographies/time horizons).

For Scope 3, explicitly list the categories included (and, if relevant, which categories are excluded) with reference to the GHG Protocol Scope 3 categories, without introducing unsupported 'unavailable data' statements.
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section provides substantial climate metrics (Scopes 1–3, financed emissions, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon price) and target/progress disclosures, but it falls short on several supported IFRS S1/S2 requirements: (i) metrics are not clearly tied to each relevant risk/opportunity; (ii) comparatives are missing for many disclosed amounts; (iii) the Scope 1 correction is not accompanied by the comparative restatement disclosures required when applicable; and (iv) IFRS S2 GHG measurement-method disclosures (GHG Protocol statement, approach/inputs/assumptions rationale, required disaggregation, and Scope 3 category listing) are incomplete.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: The reporting boundary is prepared on a financial control basis.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Claims register marks supported but provides no evidence_sources. Evidence_items include bank.boundary_type = "financial_control", but that path is not cited in the claim’s evidence_sources, so support is not properly evidenced per the provided register.

unsupported_claims.location_in_draft: Table 1: Operational GHG emissions (tCO₂e), reporting year 2024
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Claims register cites unrelated metadata paths (e.g., pcaf_methodology, risk_rating_methodology) and does not cite a Scope 2 location-based KPI value. Evidence_items list scope2_market but not scope2_location; therefore the specific numeric value is not evidenced in the provided evidence set.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Scope 3 emissions – business travel for 2024 were 289.9 tCO₂e.
unsupported_claims.location_in_draft: Table 1: Operational GHG emissions (tCO₂e), reporting year 2024
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Claims register cites unrelated target scope fields and metadata; no evidence item is provided for a business travel Scope 3 KPI value. The numeric value 289.9 is therefore not evidenced.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: For corporate loans, financed emissions are calculated by attributing a share of a borrower's total GHG emissions to the bank based on the bank's outstanding amount relative to the borrower's EVIC, and applying that share to the borrower's total GHG emissions.
unsupported_claims.location_in_draft: ### Methodology for financed emissions (bullet: Corporate loans)
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Claims register cites financed_emissions[*].total_loans_meur, which does not evidence the EVIC-based attribution methodology. Evidence_items do contain metadata.pcaf_methodology.corporate_loans describing the formula, but that path is not cited for this claim.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Internal carbon prices are used as decision-support inputs and are expressed in EUR per tCO₂e.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Claims register cites unrelated metadata/target scope fields and does not cite any evidence item that states the unit or that these prices are used as decision-support inputs. The internal_carbon_price evidence items show values and flags but not the narrative purpose/unit statement.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Target TGT001 ... status is on track.
questionable_claims.location_in_draft: ### Target TGT001 — Scope 1 and Scope 2 absolute emissions reduction
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Evidence cited supports progress %, but no evidence item is shown for the qualitative status label "on track". If status is derived from internal logic, that logic/evidence should be referenced.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions intensity target ... validated by UNEP FI.
questionable_claims.location_in_draft: ### Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions intensity reduction target
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Evidence cited covers milestones/progress fields but does not show a validation source field for UNEP FI in the provided evidence_items. Third-party validation claims typically require an explicit evidence field or reference.

questionable_claims.location_in_draft: ### Target TGT001 — Scope 1 and Scope 2 absolute emissions reduction
questionable_claims.why_questionable: As above, the provided evidence_items do not show an SBTi validation field; support depends on unseen target metadata. Needs explicit evidence path/value.

questionable_claims.claim_text: All-scopes target ... baseline 120,000.0 (baseline year/period not stated).
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Even if baseline value is evidenced, the baseline year/period is missing in the narrative, reducing interpretability and potentially failing target disclosure completeness expectations.

evidence_judge.summary: Several numeric and methodological statements are not properly evidenced by the provided evidence paths/items (notably boundary basis, Scope 2 location-based, Scope 3 business travel, corporate-loan EVIC methodology, and internal carbon pricing definition). Some target validation/status statements are also questionable without explicit evidence. Fix by adding the missing KPI evidence items and correcting evidence-source mappings to the appropriate payload paths, and by evidencing or qualifying third-party validation and status labels.

voice_issues: Voice is consistently neutral and descriptive; however, it does not explicitly adopt a single POV (first-person plural vs third-person) as suggested by the global style guide. This is a minor issue because the section avoids 'we' entirely and remains consistent in third-person descriptive voice.

Some sentences could use more standards-oriented verbs (e.g., 'disclose', 'report', 'measure') to align even more closely with IFRS-style wording, but current phrasing is acceptable and non-promotional.
structure_issues: Headings are not numbered (e.g., '1.4 Metrics and Targets', '1.4.1 Operational GHG emissions') as required by the formatting rules that call for a consistent two-level numbered hierarchy aligned to IFRS pillars.

The section opens directly with '## Metrics and Targets' and a short overview, which is good, but it does not explicitly separate general sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) from climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2) as requested in the section_style paragraph_style guidance.

Most subsections have a clear purpose statement, but some do not close with a short 'connectivity' sentence linking to related sections or financial statements (e.g., operational GHG emissions, financed emissions, internal carbon pricing).

The 'Reporting period and boundary' subsection is present and clear, but it could more explicitly distinguish between operational boundary and financed emissions boundary to fully match the 'boundary → inputs → calculation → outputs → limitations → governance' pattern described in the section_style.

The 'Internal carbon pricing' table includes duplicate 'Investment decisions' rows without an explicit explanation of how they differ (e.g., different use cases or time horizons). This is more a clarity/structure issue than a style violation, but it may confuse readers.
wording_issues: Some sentences are slightly more narrative than strictly definitional (e.g., 'For scale, total assets for 2024 were...'), though they remain neutral and non-promotional. This is acceptable but could be tightened to a more standards-led phrasing (e.g., 'Total assets for 2024 are disclosed as a scale reference for the exposure metric.').

The section generally uses clear, short-to-medium sentences and avoids promotional language. However, it could more consistently use preferred disclosure verbs (disclose, define, measure, calculate, report, present) in place of generic verbs like 'are used' or 'are presented' to fully align with the style guide.

Forward-looking or intent language is minimal, which is good, but where 'planned use of carbon credits' is mentioned, it could explicitly signal that this is an intention and may be subject to change (e.g., 'is intended to be met' or 'is planned, subject to review').

The 'All-scopes target (whole entity)' subsection does not define the baseline metric (e.g., whether the '120,000.0' is tCO₂e or another unit). This is a clarity/traceability issue rather than tone, but it affects audit-readiness.
table_figure_issues: All tables are numbered and captioned clearly (Table 1–5) and are introduced in nearby narrative, which aligns well with the style guide.
Numeric values are right-aligned and labels left-aligned, consistent with the formatting rules. Units are generally clear in captions (e.g., tCO₂e, EUR/tCO₂e, €m).

Table 3 ('Listed equity holdings') repeats the same asset class, year, currency, and proxy input basis across rows without an explicit aggregation or total row. While not strictly a style violation, adding a total or clarifying that these are sub-portfolios would improve traceability.

Table 4 ('Internal carbon prices and application') includes two rows with the same 'Application' label ('Investment decisions') but different prices and application flags. Without a clarifying note, this may appear inconsistent or duplicative.

Table 5 ('Emissions data quality and estimation mix') is clear and well-structured, but the section does not explicitly state whether these percentages apply to operational emissions, financed emissions, or all emissions metrics. A short clarifying sentence or footnote would improve alignment with the 'boundary and scope' expectations.
No figures are used, which is acceptable given the section length, but the style guide allows optional figures for boundary reconciliation; their absence is not a defect.
required_fixes: Introduce a numbered heading structure consistent with the global formatting rules (e.g., '4. Metrics and Targets', '4.1 Reporting period and boundary', '4.2 Operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions', '4.3 Financed emissions (Scope 3 Category 15)', etc.), ensuring alignment with the overall IFRS pillar hierarchy used in the report.

Explicitly distinguish climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2) from any broader sustainability metrics (IFRS S1), even if in this section all metrics are climate-related. This can be done via a short clarifying sentence in the opening paragraph (e.g., 'This section discloses climate-related metrics and targets in line with IFRS S2; broader sustainability metrics are disclosed in [Section: Metrics – Sustainability].').

Add brief 'connectivity' closing sentences to major subsections (e.g., operational GHG emissions, financed emissions, internal carbon pricing, targets) that reference related sections or appendices (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Risk Management – Climate] for how these metrics inform risk assessment.').

Clarify the unit and definition of the baseline for the 'All-scopes target (whole entity)' (e.g., specify whether '120,000.0' is tCO₂e, an index value, or another metric) and, if applicable, define the boundary and scope for this target in line with the other target descriptions.

For Table 4, either (a) differentiate the two 'Investment decisions' rows with more precise labels (e.g., 'Investment decisions – portfolio A' vs 'Investment decisions – portfolio B') or (b) add a short explanatory note describing why multiple internal carbon prices are applied to investment decisions and how they differ.

For Table 3 and Table 5, add a short clarifying sentence or footnote specifying the scope of the data: for Table 3, whether the listed equity holdings represent the full portfolio or a subset; for Table 5, whether the data quality mix applies to operational emissions, financed emissions, or all emissions metrics disclosed.

Optionally, strengthen IFRS-style wording by incorporating more of the preferred disclosure verbs in key sentences (e.g., 'We report operational GHG emissions to monitor...', 'Financed emissions are calculated and disclosed using approaches aligned to the PCAF Standard.'). This is not strictly required for approval but would further align with the style guide.
style_judge.summary: The section is well-structured, neutral, and largely aligned with the approved IFRS-style authoring guidance. It uses clear tables, concise narrative, and avoids promotional language. Key improvements needed are mostly structural and clarity-related: adopting a numbered heading hierarchy, adding connectivity sentences, clarifying certain metric definitions and scopes (especially the all-scopes target baseline, internal carbon pricing rows, and data quality coverage), and more explicitly distinguishing climate metrics from broader sustainability metrics. No reference-company content is present, and evidence discipline is strong, so the section is approved with minor revisions recommended for full style alignment.
